</details>

Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is safe for the narrow gate of running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

**Top-level scope analysis:** The PKGBUILD only defines standard packaging variables (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, arch, depends, etc.) and source/checksum arrays. There is no `pkgver()` function — `pkgver` is hardcoded as `2026.7.1`. No `eval`, no command substitution, no obfuscated content, and no download-and-execute patterns at the top level.

**Source array analysis:** All sources fetch from the project's own upstream repository on GitHub (`mountain-loop/yaak`):
- The LICENSE file from `raw.githubusercontent.com/mountain-loop/yaak/refs/tags/v${pkgver}/LICENSE`
- The pre-compiled `.deb` packages from `github.com/mountain-loop/yaak/releases/download/v${pkgver}/...`

These are pinned to the specific release tag `v${pkgver}`. Checksums (`b2sums`) are provided and populated — not SKIPped. This is fully standard packaging for a prebuilt binary distribution.

**Out of scope for this gate:** The `prepare()` (extracts deb), `build()` (sed on desktop file), and `package()` (copies files) functions are not executed by `--nobuild --noprepare`. They contain only routine packaging operations consistent with distributing a prebuilt `.deb` package.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard prebuilt binary package with pinned upstream sources and checksums.</summary>
</security_assessment>
